recommendation.justification: Satellite data shows critical vegetation health (NDVI 0.154, NDWI -0.204) indicating severe water deficit. actions: Activate the existing drip‑irrigation system and apply 25 mm of water per hectare today; repeat every 7‑10 days, adjusting to maintain soil moisture at 70‑80% of field capacity.
Supplement irrigation for the next 3 days to mimic rainfall (≈20 mm/day) to quickly raise soil moisture for the critical fruiting stage.
Incorporate 5 t ha⁻¹ of well‑decomposed compost or manure to raise organic carbon and improve water‑holding capacity; spread and lightly incorporate into the top 15 cm.
Apply a balanced NPK 10:10:10 fertilizer at 200 kg ha⁻¹ (split into two applications 7 days apart) to address the nitrogen excess and provide phosphorus and potassium for fruit development.
Conduct a visual scout for anthracnose and powdery mildew; if symptoms appear, apply a registered fungicide according to label rates.
Record soil moisture with a handheld probe daily and log irrigation volumes.
Schedule a UAV or satellite NDVI capture in 7 days to assess canopy recovery.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Soil moisture will return to optimal levels, NDVI should rise above 0.45 within two weeks, and the mango trees will resume normal vegetative growth, preserving expected yield and enabling the farmer to sell fruit at the current high market prices.

Monthly: Review market price trends and adjust harvest/marketing plan accordingly.

steps.finding: Implement immediate drip irrigation to relieve severe water stress and improve soil organic carbon while preparing for the fruiting stage.
actions: Activate the existing drip‑irrigation system and apply 25 mm of water per hectare today; repeat every 7‑10 days, adjusting to maintain soil moisture at 70‑80% of field capacity.
Supplement irrigation for the next 3 days to mimic rainfall (≈20 mm/day) to quickly raise soil moisture for the critical fruiting stage.
Incorporate 5 t ha⁻¹ of well‑decomposed compost or manure to raise organic carbon and improve water‑holding capacity; spread and lightly incorporate into the top 15 cm.
Apply a balanced NPK 10:10:10 fertilizer at 200 kg ha⁻¹ (split into two applications 7 days apart) to address the nitrogen excess and provide phosphorus and potassium for fruit development.
Conduct a visual scout for anthracnose and powdery mildew; if symptoms appear, apply a registered fungicide according to label rates.
Record soil moisture with a handheld probe daily and log irrigation volumes.
Schedule a UAV or satellite NDVI capture in 7 days to assess canopy recovery.
steps.justification: Satellite data shows critical vegetation health (NDVI 0.154, NDWI -0.204) indicating severe water deficit. Weather reports confirm zero rainfall, high humidity (88%) and wind speeds above the safe limit, compounding stress. Soil analysis reveals optimal pH and texture but low organic carbon, which can further reduce water retention. Market trends are strongly favorable, so rapid corrective action will protect yield and capture high prices.
